# Instructions for accurately documenting failed advertised specifications in a consumer product performance report

1. Start with the test records.

completion:
State the advertised specifications clearly.
3. Detail the testing methods and equipment used.
4. Record the conditions under which the product was tested, including environmental conditions.
5. Perform multiple tests if necessary for accuracy.
6. Document the test results accurately.
7. Compare the test results against the advertised specifications.
8. Highlight any discrepancies between the advertised specifications and actual test performances. Be precise about what was not met, using quantitative data when available.
9. Include graphs, charts, and visual aids to support the data and make the discrepancies clear.
10. Provide contextual information related to deviations (if applicable) such as operator error, equipment malfunction, or abnormal conditions.
11. Include data on average and variation in performance results to show consistency or lack thereof.
12. Be objective and factual in the analysis. Avoid personal opinion and focus on empirical data.
